A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A and B are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original jailbreak experiments, attack ablations, and trojan-detection evaluations in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet evaluations, including prompt-component comparisons.

M1.justification: v3 introduces a GPT-4o-specific prompt with revised instructions and a system/user message split (Section 4.3, Table 7). This is a limited model-specific adaptation; the underlying random search, self-transfer, prefilling, and trojan-detection procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 50 curated AdvBench behaviors and the same SaTML trojan-detection task. GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet extend target-model configurations without introducing different datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: The external comparator membership is unchanged after matching expanded method names and corresponding experiments across the main text and appendix. The standard GPT-4 PAP result disappears from the main GPT table but remains in v3 Table 21; it is not a removed comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds GPT-4o-2024-05-13 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet target configurations and evaluates customized system/user prompting for GPT-4o. Sections 4.3 and 6 revise reported GPT logprob access from top-5 to top-20, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. The request set and judging criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a GPT-4o comparison testing the need for prompt customization (Table 3) and extends request-structure and restart ablations to Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Tables 15–17). Existing convergence, suffix-length, judge-comparison, and false-positive analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The reporting practices are unchanged: Claude experiments retain the existing restart grids, and Figure 3 retains the 1,000-query nondeterminism demonstration. New model rows follow these practices; neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New GPT-4-judged results include GPT-4o success rates of 0%, 72%, and 100% for the original prompt, customized prompt, and full customized attack, respectively. Claude 3.5 Sonnet adds 96% transfer and 100% prefilling results plus ablation entries. All matched percentages in v2 Table 22 and v3 Table 21 remain unchanged, including GPT-4 Turbo at 96%; trojan scores are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The jailbreak feasibility formulation in Section 3.1 and the embedding-distance ranking and candidate-set definitions in Section 5 are unchanged. There are no added or revised proofs, theoretical assumptions, or mathematical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the headline from nearly 100% to 100% success while replacing GPT-4 with GPT-4o among highlighted targets and extending the Claude claims to version 3.5. The adaptivity thesis and competition-winning contribution remain unchanged. GPT-4 Turbo's retained 96% result has not improved.

C2.justification: v3 removes the explicit API-to-ChatGPT transfer limitation, the Outlook discussion of copyright, prompt injection, and scaling, and the suggested association between fewer Claude refusals and jailbreak vulnerability. Warnings about judge false positives remain in other main-text passages and Appendix B.5, so they have not disappeared altogether.

D1.justification: New Table 7 documents the full GPT-4o template, its message-role arrangement, and manual logprob-guided refinement on one example; Section 4.3 identifies its checkpoint. Existing hardware/runtime details and repository availability statements remain. Appendix B.4 replaces its direct artifact-directory URL with a less specific reference to the code.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations for Anil et al.'s many-shot jailbreaking and Liao and Sun's AmpleGCG, while removing Takemoto's attack discussion and the OpenAI journalism reference associated with the deleted Outlook. The overall research positioning remains stable. Anthropic's prefilling documentation moves from a footnote to the bibliography.

P1.justification: v3 adds Contributions and Insights labels, clarifies customization per model, reorders the self-transfer and transfer descriptions, and expands attack acronyms. It also removes the Outlook, Ethics Statement, and portions of the limitations and acknowledgements. Most prose and the main section and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document is extensively retypeset with changed typography, margins, headings, and float placement. v2 Tables 3 and 4 merge into v3 Table 2; the full-width prompt table becomes a side-by-side Figure 1; the original Figure 1 screenshot moves to Appendix B as Figure 5. A customized-prompt table and new result rows are added, while existing plots and screenshots retain their content.

improvement.justification: The GPT-4o prompt comparison adds useful evidence for the central adaptivity argument, supported by a documented template, while Claude 3.5 ablations test the existing conclusions on a newer target. These are limited gains because the earlier methods and results largely persist. Removing the API-to-ChatGPT caveat weakens scope clarification, and the stronger headline reflects changed highlighted models rather than improvement over GPT-4 Turbo's retained 96%. On balance, the targeted evidence provides a modest quality improvement.
